module_title: Mechanisms: Enzymatic Digestion, Lung Volumes & The Cardiac Cycle
introduction: This level drives into the dynamic physiological processes. It details the enzymatic cascades that break down macromolecules, the mechanics and measurable volumes of human respiration, and the precise electrical and mechanical events that constitute one heartbeat.

core_concepts.title: Physiology of Digestion
core_concepts.description:
1. Mouth: Salivary amylase (pH 6.8) breaks starch into Maltose (30% of starch is digested here).
2. Stomach: HCl (pH 1.8) activates Pepsinogen to Pepsin. Pepsin breaks proteins into proteoses and peptones. 
3. Small Intestine: Receives Pancreatic juice, Bile, and Intestinal juice (Succus entericus). 
- Pancreatic Enzymes: Trypsinogen is activated by Enterokinase (secreted by intestinal mucosa) into Trypsin. Trypsin activates chymotrypsinogen and procarboxypeptidases. Pancreatic amylase digests carbs, lipases digest fats, and nucleases digest nucleic acids.
- Bile: Contains no enzymes. Contains bile salts (bilirubin, biliverdin) for emulsification of fats (breaking into micelles) and activation of lipases.
- Succus Entericus: Contains brush border enzymes (Maltase, Dipeptidases, Lipases, Nucleosidases) that perform the final steps of digestion, converting polymers into absorbable monomers (e.g., proteins to amino acids, complex carbs to glucose).

core_concepts.title: Mechanism of Breathing
core_concepts.description:
1. Inspiration: Active process. Diaphragm contracts (moves down, increasing AP axis volume). External intercostal muscles contract (lifting ribs/sternum, increasing DV axis volume). Intrapulmonary pressure drops below atmospheric pressure, air rushes in.
2. Expiration: Passive process. Diaphragm and external intercostals relax, returning to normal positions. Intrapulmonary pressure exceeds atmospheric pressure, air is expelled.

core_concepts.title: Respiratory Volumes and Capacities
core_concepts.description:
- Tidal Volume (TV): Normal breathing volume ($500 \text{ mL}$).
- Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV): Extra volume inspired forcibly ($2500 - 3000 \text{ mL}$).
- Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV): Extra volume expired forcibly ($1000 - 1100 \text{ mL}$).
- Residual Volume (RV): Volume remaining in lungs even after forcible expiration ($1100 - 1200 \text{ mL}$).
- Vital Capacity (VC): Maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration (ERV + TV + IRV).
- Total Lung Capacity (TLC): RV + ERV + TV + IRV.

core_concepts.title: The Cardiac Cycle & ECG
core_concepts.description:
One complete heartbeat lasts $0.8 \text{ seconds}$ (assuming 72 beats/min).
1. Joint Diastole ($0.4 \text{ s}$): All 4 chambers relaxed. AV valves open, blood flows from veins to atria to ventricles.
2. Atrial Systole ($0.1 \text{ s}$): SAN generates an action potential. Atria contract, pushing the remaining 30% of blood into ventricles.
3. Ventricular Systole ($0.3 \text{ s}$): AVN transmits action potential to ventricles. Ventricles contract. AV valves close (First Heart Sound: 'Lub'). Pressure rises, Semilunar valves open, blood is pumped into aorta/pulmonary artery. Ventricles relax (Diastole), Semilunar valves close (Second Heart Sound: 'Dub').
- Electrocardiograph (ECG): P wave (Atrial depolarization/contraction). QRS complex (Ventricular depolarization/contraction). T wave (Ventricular repolarization/relaxation).

important_entities.name: Blood Grouping (ABO and Rh)
important_entities.key_fact: Based on the presence of antigens on RBCs and antibodies in plasma.
important_entities.significance: Blood group O has no antigens on RBCs but has both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in plasma (Universal Donor). Blood group AB has both A and B antigens on RBCs but no antibodies in plasma (Universal Recipient). Rh factor (Rhesus antigen) must also match. Rh incompatibility in pregnancy (Rh- mother, Rh+ fetus) can lead to Erythroblastosis foetalis (prevented by administering anti-Rh antibodies/RhoGAM to the mother after the first delivery).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A spirometer is a clinical device used to measure lung volumes to assess pulmonary functions. However, a standard spirometer CANNOT measure Residual Volume (RV), because RV is the air permanently trapped in the lungs that cannot be exhaled. Consequently, any capacity that includes RV (like Total Lung Capacity or Functional Residual Capacity) cannot be measured directly by simple spirometry.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation:
To remember the exact sequence of the heart's electrical conduction system:
**S**AN (Sino-Atrial Node, the Pacemaker)
**A**VN (Atrio-Ventricular Node)
**B**undle of His (AV Bundle)
**P**urkinje Fibers

exam_strategy_tips: In digestion, pay close attention to the absorption of fats. Fatty acids and glycerol are insoluble in water; they cannot be absorbed directly into the blood. They are first incorporated into small droplets called Micelles, enter the intestinal mucosa, and are repackaged into protein-coated fat globules called Chylomicrons, which are then transported into the lymph vessels (Lacteals) in the villi.
